purpose: This medication is used to treat symptoms of menopause, such as hot flashes, night sweats, and vaginal dryness. It can also help prevent thinning of the bones (osteoporosis) in women who have gone through menopause. It is typically prescribed for women who still have their uterus.
how_it_works: This medicine contains two female hormones — estrogen and a progestin — that your body makes less of after menopause. The estrogen helps relieve uncomfortable menopause symptoms by replacing what your body is no longer producing on its own. The progestin is included to protect the lining of your uterus, since taking estrogen alone could cause problems there.
common_side_effects: Breast tenderness or swelling, headaches, nausea, bloating, mood changes, irregular vaginal bleeding or spotting (especially in the first few months), and fluid retention. Some women also notice weight changes or decreased sex drive.
warnings: Important: This medication carries serious risks including a higher chance of breast cancer, blood clots, stroke, and heart attack, especially with long-term use. It should not be used if you have a history of blood clots, stroke, certain cancers, or unexplained vaginal bleeding. Use the lowest dose for the shortest time needed. Regular check-ups and mammograms are very important while taking this medicine.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one tablet taken by mouth once daily. Prempro comes in different strengths, so your doctor will choose what is right for you. Take it at the same time each day, with or without food. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
